question: On $\mathbb{Z}^{+}$, an operation $*$ is defined by $a*b=a-b$. Determine whether $*$ is a binary operation on $\mathbb{Z}^{+}$. Justify your answer.

options.A: $*$ is a binary operation because the difference of two positive integers is always a positive integer
options.B: $*$ is a binary operation only when $a>b$
options.C: $*$ is not a binary operation because, for example, $3*5=-2\notin\mathbb{Z}^{+}$
options.D: $*$ is not a binary operation only because subtraction is not commutative
